name: Backend Engineer
target: Backend and distributed-systems roles with no AI framing required.

content.summary: Backend engineer who takes production systems from schema to deployment — async Python services, queue-backed workers, Postgres at scale and dual-cloud infrastructure. Owns the architecture, HLD/LLD and deployment design for five platforms now running in government production, including a citizen-facing service on kheloindia.gov.in and a ~60,000-LOC platform built solo. Engineers for correctness under load: connection pooling, idempotency, transaction lifetimes and test-gated releases.

experience.employer: EY (deployed to National e-Governance Division, MeitY)
experience.context: Lead a team of 4 interns and 1 analyst. Backend and platform engineering for Government of India digital services — Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Sports Authority of India, and Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

blocks.title: Khelo India Knowledge Assistant — live in production on kheloindia.gov.in

bullets.text: Built the async FastAPI service and background worker behind a citizen-facing platform: Service Bus job queue, Redis pub/sub token relay and SSE streaming, plus two-layer caching, idempotency keys and 14 runtime feature flags including an instant kill switch needing no redeploy.

Ran Redis in OSS cluster mode with a hash-tagged keyspace for same-slot multi-key reads; modelled capacity at 10,000 daily users / 20,000 chats per hour and cut run-rate ~60% (₹9.4L → ₹3.5L per month) by re-architecting the stack. 532 offline tests.

blocks.title: PQ-Bot — document intelligence platform · MYAS / Sports Authority of India

bullets.text: Sole engineer on a ~60,000-LOC Python service — 95 REST endpoints, 34 Postgres tables, 33 Alembic migrations, 144 config settings — piloted during the 2026 Parliament monsoon session.

Tuned the concurrency model for high fan-out — raised anyio worker limits, a shared fan-out executor, a 50-connection upstream pool and explicit transaction release before long blocking calls so idle-in-transaction timeouts cannot kill connections.

blocks.title: MYAS Task Tracker & Khelo India Expenditure Tracker — internal platforms, in production

bullets.text: Authored the architecture, HLD/LLD and deployment design, then re-platformed from EC2 + PM2 onto ECS Fargate (ARM64) + RDS Postgres 16 + ALB/WAF — private subnets with NAT egress, autoscaling 1–6 tasks at 60% target CPU and Secrets Manager injection.

Built a GitHub OIDC CI/CD pipeline with no stored AWS keys: typecheck / lint / audit gate, Buildx ARM64 image with layer cache, and migrations run as a one-off in-VPC Fargate task that aborts the deploy on non-zero exit. Expenditure platform tracks ₹924 Cr across 14 regional centres.

experience.context: Oracle Cloud Partner — 20+ enterprise clients including Aditya Birla Group, Adani, and Acko.

bullets.text: Architected a Docker + GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline on AWS EC2 + Nginx, cutting deploy time 80% (15 min to under 3) with zero-downtime rolling releases, saving ~2 hrs of manual effort per cycle.

Engineered a real-time inventory backend (Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis) automating 3 reconciliation workflows, eliminating ~4 hrs/day of ops overhead, and consolidating 15+ scattered permission checks into one JWT RBAC middleware layer.

experience.context: Ed-tech platform delivering courses in web development, ML, and embedded systems to students across India.

bullets.text: Reduced frontend render latency by ~28% on a live multi-user ML platform (React DevTools Profiler) via React.memo and lazy loading — zero backend changes, zero regressions.
Built vendor-agnostic normalisation adapters over third-party ML APIs, fully decoupling business logic from vendor schemas and making future API swaps non-breaking.

projects.title: 8Byte — Real-Time Portfolio & Stock Tracking Platform   Node.js · Redis Streams · WebSockets · PostgreSQL · AWS

bullets.text: Scaled an event-driven market data pipeline to 300+ events/sec across three upstream sources via Redis Streams workers with multi-source fallback and rate-limited batching — zero event loss under peak load.
